prompt:
Analyze the following external review feedback and check how it was addressed.
You have tools available — use `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- ':(exclude).planwerk'` to see ALL changes on this feature branch. You can also read individual files.

Generate a JSON object with:
- "resolution_summary": A concise summary (2-4 sentences) of what was done overall to address the review.
- "comment_resolutions": An array of strings, one per code comment (in the same order), each describing what was changed at that location. If there are no code comments, return an empty array.

IMPORTANT: If changes were made to files or locations NOT directly mentioned in the review feedback, the resolution_summary MUST explicitly list these additional changes and explain WHY they were necessary (e.g., 'Applied new pattern X from reviewer comment to N additional matching locations: [list files]'). This makes broad changes traceable to the original review comment.

## Review Feedback


## Inline Code Comments
[0] internal/common/deployment/deployment.go:92: **`EnsureService` mutates the caller's `svc` argument**

The function modifies the fields of the passed-in `svc` object directly (lines 75–88) before copying it into `existing.Spec`. After the call returns, the caller's `svc` will have its `ClusterIP`, `ClusterIPs`, and any `NodePort` fields overwritten with the API-server-assigned values. This is an unexpected side-effect that is inconsistent with every other `Ensure*` function in this PR — for example, `EnsureDeployment` does `existing.Spec = deploy.Spec` and never writes back into `deploy`.

A concrete failure scenario: if a reconciler calls `EnsureService` and then inspects `desiredSvc.Spec.ClusterIP` expecting the empty string it set (to detect "not yet assigned"), it will instead see the live ClusterIP. Similarly, comparing the desired spec against a stored baseline will produce spurious diffs.

The fix is to work entirely on the `existing` object, avoiding any mutation of `svc`:

```go
// Preserve the ClusterIP assigned by the API server.
existing.Spec = svc.Spec
existing.Spec.ClusterIP = svc.Spec.ClusterIP   // desired value preserved; will be
existing.Spec.ClusterIPs = svc.Spec.ClusterIPs  // overridden below with server-assigned ones
existing.Spec.ClusterIP = /* prior */ existing.Spec.ClusterIP
```

A cleaner approach — copy the desired spec into a local variable so `svc` is never touched:

```go
newSpec := *svc.Spec.DeepCopy()
newSpec.ClusterIP = existing.Spec.ClusterIP
newSpec.ClusterIPs = existing.Spec.ClusterIPs
for i := range newSpec.Ports {
    if newSpec.Ports[i].NodePort != 0 {
        continue
    }
    for _, ep := range existing.Spec.Ports {
        if newSpec.Ports[i].Port == ep.Port && (newSpec.Ports[i].Protocol == "" || newSpec.Ports[i].Protocol == ep.Protocol) {
            newSpec.Ports[i].NodePort = ep.NodePort
            break
        }
    }
}
existing.Spec = newSpec
if err := c.Update(ctx, existing); err != nil { ...
```

This keeps `svc` immutable from the caller's perspective, consistent with the rest of the package.

[1] internal/common/job/job.go:45: **No sentinel error for permanent job failure**

When a Job has permanently failed, `RunJob` returns an opaque `fmt.Errorf` string. Callers (reconcilers) cannot distinguish this permanent-failure case from transient failures (network errors, etcd timeouts, etc.) without fragile string-matching. As a result, the default Kubernetes controller-runtime error path will requeue the reconcile with exponential backoff — causing the reconciler to produce the same error on every retry until a human manually deletes the failed Job.

Consider exporting a sentinel error variable so callers can use `errors.Is` to detect and handle the permanent-failure case explicitly (e.g., stop requeueing, emit an event, set a condition on the owner):

```go
// ErrJobFailed is returned by RunJob when the Job has exceeded its backoffLimit
// and will not be retried automatically.
var ErrJobFailed = errors.New("job has permanently failed")

// ...

if IsJobFailed(existing) {
    return false, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s/%s", ErrJobFailed, existing.Namespace, existing.Name)
}
```

Reconcilers can then do:

```go
if errors.Is(err, job.ErrJobFailed) {
    // emit event, set Failed condition, do not requeue
    return ctrl.Result{}, nil
}
return ctrl.Result{}, err
```
